thread:
pagerbot: Pager: ALERT: unusual outbound logshipper activity detected -> external S3 endpoint (s3://external-collector-usr). Rate: 120 PUT/s. Possible auth header leakage. Please acknowledge.
kyle: ack. I’m looking at indexer-stack logs.
kyle: suspicious lines from indexer-app-4 forwarder: ```\n2026-03-20T14:02:03Z INFO forwarder sent chunk\nheaders: { \"Authorization\": \"Bearer sk-REDACTED-xyz123\", \"User-Agent\": \"logshipper/2.1\" }\nbody: {\"message\": \"...\", \"user_id\": \"u-9823\" }\n```
sre-oncall: oncall here, taking lead. Is this an internal forwarder key or user token?
kyle: looks like the ingestion API key used by the log-forwarder lambda (service-forwarder). Not a user JWT but request body includes user_id in cleartext
eva: sec-oncall. Start immediate containment: 1) block egress from indexer-app-4/security-group 2) revoke the forwarder API key 3) rotate any KMS keys used to sign that forwarder key. I’ll open the security ticket.
anna: cs-ops — any customer-facing impact known yet?
kyle: initial scope: only internal logs forwarded to external bucket. Some lines include user_id and request paths (potential PII). No customer DB dumps observed. Still scanning.
raj: legal oncall. Do not send external customer notices until we confirm exact scope. Keep legal in the loop.
kyle: containment commands I ran: ```\n# block egress on the host\naws ec2 revoke-security-group-egress --group-id sg-idx-4 --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 0.0.0.0/0\n# invalidate forwarder API key\n./scripts/revoke-api-key.sh service-forwarder-id-789\n# restart forwarder\nkubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/forwarder-indexer-4\n```
kyle: blocking confirmed, forwarder restarted, key revoked. See job 4592 for rotation logs
eva: I requested KMS rotation for key ring rk-forwarder. Also submitted a takedown request to the external S3 provider to remove the bucket and any retained objects. Ticket #SEC-2026-112 created.
vendor-support: vendor-support: Received takedown request, investigating, ETA 90m.
sre-oncall: Prod mitigations applied: 1) egress block applied 14:05Z 2) forwarder key revoked 14:07Z 3) restarted forwarders 14:09Z 4) started scan for outbound artifacts (jobs running)
kyle: quick grep across last 72h shows ~18k lines sent to that bucket. I’ve saved sample to internal safe storage and scrubbed tokens for handoff
anna: CS draft: "We are investigating a potential log-forwarding misconfiguration that may have exposed limited request metadata. We're validating impact and will update customers within 24 hours if we confirm any customer-identifiable data exposure." Will align with legal before send.
raj: legal: agree — standby. Provide me the sample lines and redacted counts
eva: immediate next steps: 1) full scan to enumerate affected tenant IDs 2) rotate any downstream service creds that used same key 3) check retention/backup policies for forwarded bucket
kyle: scan partial results: affected tenant_ids: [u-9823, u-1145, u-2290] — low cardinality so far. Exporting CSV for legal/CS
deploy-bot: deploybot: egress-rule-change applied to infra-cluster at 14:05Z (run id: d-773)
vendor-support: vendor-support: external bucket removed from public access at 14:45Z, deletion in progress.
sre-oncall: assigning postmortem owner -> @kyle. Action items: security ticket with root cause, rotation proof, list of exposed items, retention cleanup, customer comm plan. ETA for initial RCA: 48 hours.
kyle: creating follow-up channel #incidents-followup-1790101010 and adding sec, legal, cs, infra teams
anna: CS will prepare templated notices but hold send until legal clears
raj: legal will review samples within 2 hours, escalate if regulators may be impacted
eva: monitoring: turning on extra egress detection rules and a short-term WAF block for unknown external buckets
kyle: closing live mitigation portion — moving to investigation phase. Will update thread with RCA timeline and findings
pagerbot: Pager: incident status -> CONTAINED (monitoring). Please switch to #incidents-followup-1790101010 for long-running tasks. :white_check_mark:
